raw_system_prompt:
You are a .NET code quality expert. You will be given a code anti-pattern finding.

Explain the impact of this anti-pattern on relevant ISO/IEC 25010 software
quality attributes. Focus on attributes such as maintainability, analysability,
modifiability, testability, security, reliability, and compatibility where
applicable. Only mention attributes that are genuinely relevant — do not
enumerate every attribute by default.

Respond ONLY with a JSON object in this exact format, with no additional text:
{
  "explanation": "<why this is a problem and what its impact is>",
  "quality_impact": "Quality impact:\n- Attribute: short explanation\n- Attribute: short explanation",
  "remediation": "<concrete refactoring steps; include a short code example where helpful>"
}
parsed_explanation: RecurrenceEngine combines recurrence expansion, occurrence lookup, holiday policy, time-zone conversion, validation, and mutable caching. Its very high complexity (WMC 48) and low cohesion (TCC 0.3) indicate that these responsibilities do not form a focused abstraction. The shared _expanded list also creates temporal coupling: NextOccurrence only works after Expand, a later Expand mutates previously returned IReadOnlyList results, and concurrent calls can corrupt or observe inconsistent state. Hard-coded fixed time-zone offsets ignore daylight-saving transitions, ambiguous/invalid local times, DateTime.Kind, and platform time-zone rules, while silent fallback to the input value hides configuration errors. These characteristics make scheduling defects difficult to isolate and can produce incorrect or nondeterministic appointments.
parsed_quality_impact:
Quality impact:
- Maintainability: Unrelated recurrence, calendar, validation, state management, and time-zone rules change in one high-complexity class, increasing coupling and regression risk.
- Analysability: Numerous guards, magic limits, silent fallbacks, and dependence on prior calls obscure control flow, invariants, and the source of incorrect schedule results.
- Modifiability: Adding recurrence patterns, regional holidays, or daylight-saving behavior requires editing the same class and can unintentionally affect unrelated functionality.
- Testability: Hidden mutable collections and call-order dependence prevent isolated, deterministic tests; time-zone and holiday policies cannot be replaced with controlled test doubles.
- Reliability: Shared mutable state is not thread-safe, returned results can change after subsequent calls, and NextOccurrence may return results from a different job. Fixed offsets and unchecked boundary arithmetic can yield wrong times or exceptions near DateTime limits.
- Compatibility: Custom CET/EST mappings do not interoperate reliably with standard system time-zone identifiers or daylight-saving rules, so results can differ from external calendar and scheduling systems.

raw_system_prompt:
You are a code-editing tool, not a code reviewer. You will be given a C# source
file, an anti-pattern finding, and a proposed repair. Apply ONLY the changes the
proposed repair explicitly specifies. Do not add improvements, do not fix
anything the repair does not mention, and do not make design decisions the repair
leaves open. If the repair is too vague to apply without inventing specifics
(e.g. "refactor to follow SRP" with no concrete partition), do not guess.

Respond ONLY with a JSON object, no additional text:
{
  "applicable": <true|false>,
  "reason_if_not": "<why the repair cannot be applied literally, or empty>",
  "edited_file": "<the full edited source if applicable, else empty>"
}
repair_unapplicable_reason: The proposed repair introduces new interfaces (IRecurrenceCalculator, IHolidayCalendar, ITimeZoneConverter) and concrete classes (RecurrenceCalculator, SystemTimeZoneConverter) that are not defined anywhere in the source file. It also changes the public API (removes ToLocal, changes NextOccurrence signature, etc.) and references a non-existent NextWorkday method. Applying the example code literally would result in a non-compilable file with missing dependencies and broken callers. The repair cannot be applied without inventing the missing types and method implementations.
